transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2029-07-16 09:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood Platform), Sarah Lopez (AuroraBank Head ML Infra), Tom Brennan (AuroraBank Lead Platform Eng), Nina Patel (AuroraBank Security)

Summary:
High-level: dig into per-tenant kernel fingerprinting in VPC deployments, investigate eviction-driven latency spikes with quantized models and CUDA graph replay fidelity across TRT-LLM and vLLM execution paths. Decide on pilot benchmarks and tracing instrumentation.

Topics: kernel selection heuristics, CUDA graphs nondeterminism, KV cache warm/cold behavior, quantization noise, multi-tenant VPC isolation, on-prem NUMA effects, trace collection plan

[00:00] Alex: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros please
[00:10] Sarah: Sarah here, head of ML infra at AuroraBank. we're exploring Redwood for inference across multi-tenant VPC clusters, curious about kernel choices and stability
[00:18] Alex: great, Alex from Redwood, i'll run the flow. Priya is our SE, focuses on runtime profiling
[00:25] Priya: hi all
[00:27] Tom: Tom here; we run mixed workloads, long-form generation and high qps rerank. latency tail is a problem when eviction kicks in

[02:10] Priya: can you describe the eviction pattern? is it memory thrash on NVMe or GPU side? any NUMA pinning?
[02:22] Tom: mostly GPU memory eviction when two tenants spike, sometimes host page faults. interestingly it correlates with quantized LLMs where prefix KV cache grows
[02:36] Marcus: is the model using persistent KV across requests? or per-inference warm-up?
[02:42] Tom: persistent for session state, yes. we pinned to the same device but when two tenants share the same GPU pool we see kernel switches

[05:00] Priya: that sounds like a classic kernel path fingerprint: runtime picks TensorRT-LLM kernels for quant path, but when eviction happens it falls back to vLLM's dynamic path which has different prefetch and cudaGraph replay characteristics
[05:18] Sarah: can you explain the cudaGraph part? we've seen cudagraph replay causing latency variance after replay failure
[05:28] Priya: sure. TRT-LLM uses more static cudagraph capture for hot paths, vLLM tends to rebuild kernels dynamically; when memory layout changes the captured graph can misalign and force fallback which is expensive

[08:40] Alex: also worth noting that quantization changes kernel selection: 4-bit/INT4 code paths use different GEMM kernels and sometimes different workspace sizes which affect eviction thresholds
[09:05] Nina: from security side, we're concerned about multi-tenant bleed via shared GPU memory pools. how do you isolate traces and keys in VPC/private?
[09:17] Alex: Redwood can deploy per-tenant queues and tenancy-aware allocation policies. for private we support VPC peering and KMS per-account. we'll share our security docs

[11:00] Priya: back to profiling—what traces can you collect? nvtx, cupti, nsight shows kernel durations and launch params; for cudagraphs we need the sequence of kernel launches across capture boundaries
[11:16] Tom: we can run Nsight and collect nvtx zones but limited on prod; staging is OK
[11:26] Priya: perfect. we'll give an instrumented docker with nvtx markers in the runtime and a script to reproduce the eviction by creating synthetic tenant load

[13:30] Sarah: does Redwood's runtime do eviction-aware batching? we want batching that doesn't amplify one tenant's spike
[13:42] Marcus: yes, we have policy routing with per-tenant quotas and a hysteresis policy to avoid batch thrash. but the kernel mapper can still choose a heavier kernel under load which increases memory footprint

[16:00] Tom: i want a concrete experiment: run TRT-LLM quantized v.s. vLLM quantized on the same node, with a background tenant producing small requests to push memory. measure tail latency and graph-replay events
[16:18] Priya: agreed. we should also toggle persistent KV on/off to see cache warm-up cost. and run NVLINK multi-gpu swap scenario to stress transient copies

[18:30] Alex: for data collection we'll ask for: kernel telemetry (timestamped), nvtx annotated traces, dmesg for OOMs, and the runtime's kernel selection logs. also workload profiles (seq len, batch, qps)
[18:44] Tom: we can provide these from staging. note our topology: 2xA100 per node, NVLINK enabled, VPC with SR-IOV and tenant namespaces

[21:00] Priya: about kernel selection heuristics—our runtime computes a cost model: latency per token vs memory footprint vs throughput. sometimes cost model picks a dynamic kernel to keep latency low but memory grows and triggers eviction; we can tune the cost weights per-tenant
[21:22] Sarah: can you tune per-tenant? we have some strict SLA tenants and some lower priority
[21:28] Marcus: yes, priority routing and memory caps per-tenant is supported, and we can restrict certain kernels for a tenant (for example force vLLM path to avoid cudagraph capture instability)

[24:50] Tom: any known nondeterminism between TRT capture and replay? we've seen replays that fail silently and lead to fallback with a 200-400ms penalty
[25:06] Priya: replay failure commonly happens when pointer addresses change due to reallocation or when workspace size differs. also when quantization changes internal buffer alignments. we add guard checks and attempt a rebuild; but rebuild is expensive
[25:36] Alex: adding to that—TRT's engine can fail if the underlying cuBLAS/cuDNN versions mismatch across nodes; for private on-prem with curated libs it's more stable

[28:10] Sarah: so what's our mitigation? pin kernel path? increase memory pool? smarter prefetch?
[28:20] Priya: mitigations: 1) enforce per-tenant memory caps 2) prefer dynamic kernels when churn is high 3) use a fallback hysteresis window to avoid repeated rebuilds 4) add kv-cache priming so all sessions avoid cold misses
[28:40] Tom: priming seems promising. how big is the priming overhead for large contexts (6k+ tokens)?
[28:50] Priya: depends; priming the KV cache for 6k can be heavy but we can checkpoint compressed caches and reuse them for sessions with similar prefixes. that's part of our cache snapshotting

[31:00] Marcus: note: on NUMA systems the PCI bus and NUMA placement can cause pointer differences that affect cudagraph capture. on-prem nodes with mixed CPUs require explicit pinning
[31:16] Tom: we saw that—without numactl pinning latency tails rose with background processes. can Redwood's installer apply numa pin settings?
[31:25] Alex: yes for private deployments we provide an install manifest that sets CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and numa policies. we'll include a recommended sysctl/numactl profile

[33:40] Sarah: about quantization—do we support hybrid quant (some layers FP16, some INT8) and how does that affect kernel selection
[33:50] Priya: hybrid quant introduces heterogenous kernels; runtime will select kernel per-layer; cost model combines these. It can increase the number of kernel transitions which increases the chance of capture mismatch

[36:00] Tom: any known differences in output quality when forcing TRT-LLM vs vLLM on quantized models? we worry about regressions
[36:10] Priya: in our internal evals quality delta is small for common prompts, but rare tokens can shift. we'll run your eval prompt set as part of the pilot

[38:20] Alex: next steps recap — we'll ship a bench harness and an instrumented runtime, you run on staging and return traces. Redwood will analyze kernel selection logs and recommend policy changes

Action items (in call):
[40:00] Alex: I'll upload the bench docker and scripts (AI-harness-trace.tar.gz)
[40:10] Priya: I'll annotate nvtx zones for KV read/write, kernel map entries, and cudagraph capture points
[40:25] Tom: I'll share VPC topology and tenant qps expectations

[42:00] Sarah: on security, Nina has questions about KMS usage and trace data retention
[42:10] Nina: we need assurance traces have PII stripped and traces stored in our S3 with lifecycle controls
[42:20] Alex: understood — Redwood supports scrub hooks and will redact payloads; we'll send SOC2 and our data handling whitepaper

[44:30] Tom: timeline — can you deliver the instrumented runtime by Friday 2029-07-19? we aim to run benchmarks next week
[44:44] Alex: yes that's feasible
[44:50] Priya: we'll include instructions for nsight and a lighter nvtx-only mode for limited staging

[46:00] Sarah: thanks everyone. any blockers?
[46:10] Tom: none from our side once we get the docker
[46:15] Nina: just security docs
[46:20] Alex: we'll follow up in email with links and schedule the on-prem install window

[47:00] Meeting end

Notes: transcript contains some transcription artifacts (speaker overlaps, misrecognized acronyms). We'll attach the raw nvtx traces as artifacts when available.
